fields.meta_title: Post Webinar Survey Builder and Question Guide | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Create a post webinar survey with the right questions, open it from any webinar tool, and send demo requests to your CRM. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Post Webinar Survey That Shapes Your Next Session
fields.hero_description: Build a post webinar survey attendees open as the session ends, with demo requests sent to your CRM and every answer saved.
fields.features_heading: What Attendees Answer and What You Get Back
fields.features_subheading: Attendees meet the first two as the webinar ends. The other four do their work after the session, up to the exported code.
fields.feature_1:
Questions written for the session you ran

Name the topic and the speakers, then say what the results should change. Emergent writes the rating and next-step questions, and you reword any of them with one more sentence.
fields.feature_2:
One link any webinar tool can open

Publish the survey once and put one link everywhere attendees look: on the closing slide, in the follow-up email, or in the redirect field of a webinar tool that offers one.
fields.feature_3:
Demo requests that land in your CRM

An attendee who ticks Book a demo becomes a contact in HubSpot or any CRM with an API, with the webinar name and their rating attached. A Slack alert names each one for sales.
fields.feature_4:
Ratings compared across a series

Each response carries the session it came from. The dashboard averages the 1-5 rating per session and per speaker, and a weak session stands out next to the others in one chart.
fields.feature_5:
No cap on how many attendees answer

Every answer becomes a row in a database you own, and no response cap applies when 4,000 people attend instead of 40. Filter by session or speaker, or join it to the registrant list.
fields.feature_6:
Code export to your own GitHub

On paid plans, Emergent exports the survey app, its dashboard, and its CRM connection to your GitHub repository. A developer on your team can review the code or keep building on it.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Webinars and What Their Surveys Found
fields.tab_content_1:
23 demo requests reach HubSpot before the replay goes out

Quillmark's product team ends its reporting webinar with a survey link on the last slide and in the follow-up email. Of 312 attendees, 104 answer. Of those, 23 tick Book a demo, and the app adds each one to HubSpot as a contact before the replay email goes out the next morning.
fields.tab_content_2:
Session 3 scores 3.6, below every other session

Corvel Learning asks the same 1-5 rating after each of the 4 sessions in its spreadsheet skills series. The dashboard lines up the averages: 4.1, 4.4, 3.6, and 4.5. Session 3, on pivot tables, is the outlier, and 14 of its comments mention the audio cutting out.
fields.tab_content_3:
61 viewers raise a hand for April's creek cleanup

Bramblecote Creek Alliance puts a QR code on the final slide of its public webinar on stream health. The survey opens on viewers' phones, one question per screen. Of 140 who answer, 61 say yes to the April creek cleanup, and the app adds them to the cleanup sign-up list.
fields.tab_content_4:
Mileage is the unclear part for 46 employees

Tinderbay Freight's HR team trains 180 drivers and dispatchers on its new expense policy by webinar. The survey asks which part of the policy is still unclear. Of 118 who answer, 46 pick mileage claims. HR books a 15-minute session on mileage alone for the following week.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Post Webinar Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a post webinar survey, build it with Emergent, and act on what attendees tell you.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what the answers will change
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the one or two decisions the survey feeds: whether to repeat the topic, which speaker to book again, or who sales calls first. Cut any question that informs none of them. Write those decisions down before you draft a single question.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Tell Emergent who attended, what the webinar covered, and what the results page should show. Emergent builds the survey, its database, and the dashboard from that description. To change a question later, ask for the change in a sentence.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Open with a 1-5 rating of the session, then ask what was most useful and what was still unclear. Add a rating per speaker when more than one person presented. Save the open comment box for last, where a skipped answer costs nothing.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Close with the action the webinar was for: a Book a demo checkbox, a seat at the next session, or a topic request. Word the demo question so that ticking it gives permission to call, and sales only contacts people who asked.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the link to 3 colleagues who skipped the webinar and ask them to answer on a phone. Watch for a question they read two ways or a scale that runs off the screen, and fix it before the live session.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Share the link as the session ends
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put the link on the closing slide as a QR code and mention it in the last 2 minutes. If your webinar tool can open a survey link when the session ends, paste it there too, and repeat it in the replay email.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Read the answers and act on them
fields.howto_step_7_des: Read the first answers within the hour and call the demo requests while the session is fresh. When the survey closes, compare the rating with your last webinar and tell attendees one thing you will change next time.

faq_plan.q: What are some good questions to include in a post-webinar survey?
faq_plan.ref: What are some good questions to include in a post-webinar survey?

prov.original: What are some good questions to include in a post-webinar survey?

faq_plan.a: Open on how attendees rate the session overall, from 1 to 5, and what they found most useful. Then ask what was still unclear, how each speaker did, and which topic they want covered next. Finish on the step the webinar was meant to drive, such as a demo request. Write each of these post webinar survey questions about the session you ran, not about webinars in general.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a post webinar survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe the webinar, its audience, and the questions you want in a plain-English prompt, and Emergent's AI survey builder turns it into a working survey with a results dashboard and a database behind it. Publish it, put the link on your closing slide and in the replay email, and edit any question later with one more prompt.

faq_plan.q: Is a post webinar survey template enough, or should each session get its own?
faq_plan.a: A post webinar survey template is a fine start for the rating and comment questions, which stay the same every time. Write the rest for the session: name the topic in the usefulness question and match the closing question to the webinar's goal. With Emergent, you describe those changes in a prompt and the survey is rebuilt to match.

faq_plan.q: How is a post-webinar survey different from one for an in-person event?
faq_plan.a: It asks about things an in-person event never has: audio and video quality, and whether attendees stayed to the end. It leaves out the venue and catering questions that a post event survey covers.

faq_plan.q: What is the best time to show a post-webinar survey to attendees?
faq_plan.a: Show it the moment the session ends, then send it again with the replay. A Zoom webinar host can schedule a survey to be sent to attendees and panelists when the webinar ends, and can redirect them to a third-party survey service instead. Close the survey after about a week, while attendees still remember the session.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a post-webinar survey have?
faq_plan.a: Keep it to 8 questions or fewer for an hour-long webinar, and about 5 for a 30-minute one. Put the rating first and the demo question last, since those two feed the next decision. Anything past that limit can go in a follow-up survey to the people who asked to hear more.

faq_plan.q: Can I run a post-webinar survey after an online class or a livestreamed service?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The core questions carry over: rate the session and say what was still unclear. For a livestreamed service, ask about the stream itself, such as sound and video, and leave questions about congregation life to a separate church survey. Emergent builds either one from a prompt, with no response cap.

faq_plan.q: Should a post-webinar survey be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Keep the ratings anonymous and the contact details optional. People rate a session more freely when their name is not attached, but a demo request is useless without a name and email. Ask for contact details only in the question where someone asks for a next step, and say so in that question.

faq_plan.q: How do I get more attendees to answer a post-webinar survey?
faq_plan.a: Ask while they are still in the session. Mention the survey before the last audience question, show the link as a QR code on the last slide, and make the first question a single tap. Send one reminder with the replay link and stop there. Each response is saved to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can a post-webinar survey sign people up for a next step like volunteering?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a yes-or-no question for the next step and have the app add each yes to a sign-up list with the person's name and email. To collect availability and preferred shifts, send a separate volunteer survey to the people who said yes instead of lengthening the webinar survey.
